items.p: What does the word 'commerce' refer to?
items.a: The distribution and sale of physical goods
items.ref: With the word 'commerce' we define the distribution and the sale of goods: it is used to talk about physical goods.

items.p: What is the word 'trade' mostly used for?
items.a: To talk about buying and selling services
items.ref: Trade refers to buying and selling services; it is mostly used to talk about services.

items.p: Which factor makes trade and commerce easier?
items.a: Innovation in technology, transport and communication
items.ref: Innovation in technology, transport and communication systems enables more contact between people and parts of the world.

items.p: Which of these is a service that supports trade?
items.a: Insurance
items.ref: Services to trade include storage, transport, distribution, insurance, banking, marketing and IT support.

items.p: What are the two types of trade?
items.a: Home trade and international trade
items.ref: Trade can be of two different types: home trade and international trade.

items.p: What is home trade?
items.a: The sale and distribution of products within one country
w: The exchange of goods between countries
items.ref: Home trade includes the sale and distribution of products within one country, from production to consumption.

items.p: Who sells goods to retailers in smaller quantities, with a markup?
items.a: Wholesalers
items.ref: Wholesalers sell goods to retailers in smaller quantities with a price markup.

items.p: At what price do final consumers buy goods?
items.a: At a retail price
items.ref: Final consumers buy goods at a retail price.

items.p: Why are retail sales an indicator of the health of an economy?
items.a: Consumers spend more in expansion and less in a recession
items.ref: In periods of expansion consumers tend to increase their spending; in periods of recession they spend less.

items.p: Which is an example of non-store retailing?
items.a: Door-to-door selling
items.ref: Non-store retailing includes businesses that do not sell from a store: door-to-door selling, distance selling and online selling.

items.p: What is international trade?
items.a: The exchange of goods and services between different countries
w: The sale of products within one country
The production of goods for the family
items.ref: International trade is the exchange of goods and services between different countries.

items.p: What is invisible trade?
items.a: The exchange of services between countries
items.ref: Invisible trade is the exchange of services between countries, such as tourism, insurance and education.

items.p: Which is a benefit of international trade for consumers?
items.a: More variety and lower prices
items.ref: Thanks to international trade consumers may benefit of more variety and lower prices.

items.p: What is the balance of trade (BOT)?
items.a: The difference between total exports and total imports
w: The money of the central bank
The number of companies in a country
items.ref: BOT is the difference between total exports and total imports over a certain period of time.

items.p: When does a country have a trade deficit?
items.a: When exports are lower than imports
w: When exports are higher than imports
items.ref: We talk about a trade deficit or trade gap when exports are lower than imports.

items.p: What does e-commerce refer to?
items.a: All the aspects of online selling
w: Only shops in the city centre
items.ref: E-commerce refers to all the functional aspects of online selling: website, transactions, payments.

items.p: Why are consumer habits changing?
items.a: Because of technology and the presence of smartphones
items.ref: The change is due to the use of technology in everyday life and to the ubiquitous presence of smartphones.

items.p: What is C2C e-commerce?
items.a: Sales between consumers, for example on eBay
items.ref: C2C is the sale between consumers directly, without a physical shop or a brand.

items.p: What is O2O commerce?
items.a: A strategy that turns online visitors into offline sales
items.ref: O2O (online to offline) turns e-commerce visitors into offline sales, for example with click and collect.

items.p: How did Amazon start in 1994?
items.a: It only sold books
w: It opened shops with no checkout
items.ref: When Amazon started in 1994, it only sold books.

items.p: What is a trade alliance?
items.a: Countries that create cheaper and freer trade with each other
w: A ban on trade with a country
items.ref: In a trade alliance, countries of the same economic group create cheaper and freer trade with each other.

items.p: Which countries are part of the USMCA?
items.a: USA, Mexico and Canada
items.ref: The USMCA includes the USA, Mexico and Canada; it replaced NAFTA in 2020.

items.p: What are trade sanctions?
items.a: Laws and regulations to limit or abolish trade with some countries
items.ref: Trade sanctions are laws and regulations to limit or even abolish trade with certain countries.

items.p: What is an embargo?
items.a: A total or partial ban on trade with a country
items.ref: An embargo is a total or partial ban on trade, imposed on specific countries.

items.p: What does a quota limit?
items.a: The quantity of a product that can be imported
items.ref: Quotas are legal restrictions on the quantity of a product that can be imported from abroad.

items.p: What is ethical trade?
items.a: Improving the working conditions of the people who produce goods
w: Selling goods at the lowest price
items.ref: Ethical trade: retailers, brands and suppliers improve the working conditions of the people who produce the goods.

items.p: Who launched the Ethical Trading Initiative?
items.a: Companies, NGOs and trade unions
items.ref: The ETI was launched in the UK in the late 1990s by a group of companies, NGOs and trade unions.

items.p: What must all ETI members adopt?
items.a: The Base Code
items.ref: All ETI members must adopt and enforce the Base Code, an international code of labour practice.

items.p: Which is a principle of the ETI Base Code?
items.a: Child labour shall not be used
w: Wages are as low as possible
items.ref: The Base Code says, for example, that child labour shall not be used and living wages are paid.

items.p: What does Fairtrade do for banana farmers?
items.a: It gives them a minimum price and a decent pay
w: It buys bananas at the lowest price
items.ref: Fairtrade works with banana farmers and workers to create more value and a decent pay; in 2023 it raised the minimum prices.
